routes.label: Complete the container to a pyramid

question:
A container has a \(1 \times 1\) square bottom, a \(3 \times 3\) open square top, and four congruent trapezoidal sides, as shown. Starting when the container is empty, a hose that runs water at a constant rate takes \(35\) minutes to fill the container up to the midline of the trapezoids.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_10B_Q19_question_fig1.svg)

How many more minutes will it take to fill the remainder of the container?
solution:
Because the hose runs at a constant rate, filling times are proportional to the volumes added. We therefore need the ratio of the upper and lower portions of the container.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_10B_Q19_question_fig1.svg)

Extend the sloping edges below the bottom to complete a square pyramid. To justify this construction, consider one trapezoidal face: extending its legs forms a triangle whose parallel sections have lengths \(1\) and \(3\). Similarity places each bottom endpoint one third as far from the triangle's vertex as the corresponding top endpoint. Adjacent faces share a sloping edge, so their constructed vertices coincide.

Let \(h>0\) be the height from this apex to the container's bottom. The parallel square sections with sides \(1\) and \(3\) are then at heights \(h\) and \(3h\). The trapezoid midlines join the midpoints of the sloping edges, so their square section is at height \(2h\) and has side length \(2\).

A pyramid's volume is one third of its base area times its height. Thus the three pyramids ending at the bottom, midline, and top have volumes
\[
\frac{1^2h}{3}=\frac h3,
\qquad
\frac{2^2(2h)}{3}=\frac{8h}{3},
\qquad
\frac{3^2(3h)}{3}=\frac{27h}{3}.
\]
Subtracting the appropriate pyramids gives
\[
V_{\text{lower}}=\frac{7h}{3},
\qquad
V_{\text{upper}}=\frac{19h}{3}.
\]
Since \(h>0\), their ratio is \(19/7\). The additional filling time is therefore
\[
35\cdot\frac{19}{7}=95\text{ minutes}.
\]
The answer is \(95\) more minutes, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
